evidence_quotes.quote: Este artigo aborda os conflitos pelo uso da água e as apropriações do setor de saneamento por novos atores, a partir do novo arcabouço legal e do contexto de mudanças climáticas

Neste artigo são levantadas questões sobre o alcance das metas do ODS 6, no contexto brasileiro, tendo como ponto de partida a promulgação da Lei Federal nº.14.026, de 15 de julho de 2020, conhecida como a revisão do Marco Legal do Saneamento Básico (Lei Federal nº 11.445 de 2007).
O estudo partiu do entendimento sobre as mudanças no marco legal do setor do saneamento, discutidas a partir do enfoque da participação, do conflito e da justiça climática.
dos serviços de abastecimento de água entre 2015 e 2018; e o aumento percentual no esgotamento sanitário foi menor, também, na segunda metade da década de 2010 (Tabela 1).
Apontam-se a participação social e o investimento público como caminhos para a superação dos déficits de acesso e efetivação dos direitos humanos à água e ao saneamento básico no país.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines public drinking-water supply and sewage/sanitation service access in Brazil under SDG 6.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 reading: This paper passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 because it discusses Brazil's sanitation legal framework (Federal Law No. 11.445/2007 and Federal Law No. 14.026/2020), private-sector appropriation/privatization, and social participation in water and sanitation governance. However, it fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading because these legal and governance themes are discussed only as macro-political and normative commentary; no specific rule-type mechanism (such as utility ownership, tariff rules, contract terms, or eligibility rules) is empirically analysed in relation to household or community service access. (Even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the paper is still excluded overall because it fails Criteria 3 and 5.)
criterion_notes.c3: No empirical research design, methods section, primary data, or systematic synthesis. The article is a theoretical and normative policy essay that cites secondary literature and reproduces descriptive macro-regional/national background charts from official portals (MCTI drought risk projections, SNIS 2010-2020 coverage, Plansab 2010-2018 national indicators, and DATASUS 2020 sanitation-related disease rates) without any empirical analysis testing legal or governance effects.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports descriptive aggregate secondary figures on household and population water supply and sewage coverage across Brazilian regions from SNIS and Plansab reports.
criterion_notes.c5: Fails to provide an identifiable empirical study design or an empirically measured legal/governance exposure linked to access outcomes; all descriptive SNIS/Plansab coverage data end in 2018-2020 (when Law No. 14.026/2020 was just enacted in July 2020) and are never disaggregated or analysed by utility ownership, regulatory structure, or participatory governance.
criterion_notes.c6: Published in Portuguese (with Portuguese and English abstracts), which is directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

study_design: Theoretical and normative policy commentary essay citing descriptive secondary official statistics (no empirical study design)
population_and_sample: General population and households in Brazil across macro-regions (secondary aggregate statistics from SNIS, Plansab, MCTI, and DATASUS; no primary sample)
exposure: Normative/policy discussion of Brazil's revised Sanitation Legal Framework (Federal Law No. 14.026/2020 amending Law No. 11.445/2007), privatization, and social participation (not empirically measured)
outcome: Descriptive national and regional public water supply and sewage coverage rates from secondary official reports (Plansab 2010-2018 and SNIS 2010-2020)
rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence). Full text in Portuguese matches record metadata (Fracalanza, da Paz, & Alves, 2023, DOI 10.5380/dma.v62i0.89421). Although the article discusses water and sanitation service access in Brazil (SDG 6) and critiques the 2020 revision of the Sanitation Legal Framework (Federal Law No. 14.026/2020), privatization, and limits on social participation, it is a theoretical and normative policy commentary with no empirical methods section, no primary data, and not a systematic synthesis. It reproduces descriptive macro-regional charts from official government portals (MCTI drought risk, SNIS 2010-2020 coverage, Plansab 2010-2018 coverage, and DATASUS 2020 disease rates) solely as contextual background, without any empirical study design or analysis connecting a rule-type legal, ownership, or governance mechanism to service access outcomes (failing Criteria 2 under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, 3, and 5; also excluded under the plain reading of Criterion 2 due to failing Criteria 3 and 5).
